title: Turning a shape is not the same as flipping it
description: Use an asymmetric shape to tell a rotation from a mirror reflection, one movement at a time.

cover.alt: A navy L-shaped wooden piece beside a mirror
cover.credit: AI-generated photorealistic image created for BrainiLab.

practice: Try a few problems at your own pace, then return to any explanation you want to revisit.

sections.title: Try it with a paper shape
sections.html:
Cut an L shape from paper. Turn it a quarter-turn on the table. Its size and outline stay the same, but it points a different way. This is a rotation.

Now imagine looking at it in a mirror. The bend changes sides. That is a reflection. A shape with a clearly marked corner makes the difference easier to notice than a plain circle would.

sections.title: Try it yourself
sections.html:
Use the quarter-turn button to rotate the L. Four quarter-turns bring it back to its starting orientation. Use the mirror button to reflect it from left to right.

Follow the small dot as well as the outside edge. The dot is attached to the shape, so it moves with it. This prevents a symmetric-looking outline from hiding what changed.

sections.title: Use the direction in the question
sections.html:
A clockwise quarter-turn follows the direction of clock hands. A half-turn rotates through two quarter-turns. A full turn is four quarter-turns, or 360 degrees.

A reflection needs a mirror line. In this activity the mirror line is vertical, so left and right switch. A horizontal mirror would switch top and bottom instead.

sections.title: Check features, not a vague impression
sections.html:
Look for a short arm, a long arm and a marked corner. Track where each feature moves. If only one feature matches your prediction, you may have turned the shape the wrong way or imagined a reflection.

Some shapes, such as a square without a mark, can look unchanged after certain movements. That does not mean no movement happened. Distinctive features make a reasoning question less ambiguous.

questions.prompt: How many quarter-turns make a full turn?
questions.explanation: Each quarter-turn is one of four equal parts of a full turn.

questions.prompt: A reflection in a vertical mirror switches…
questions.explanation: The mirror reverses left and right relative to its vertical line.

questions.prompt: Why add a dot to a shape?
options: To track a specific part during movement
questions.explanation: The mark helps distinguish movements that otherwise look similar.
